title: The Warm room in winter
subtitle: 天气气候 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）
meta: 主题语境：天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）　|　核心词汇：warm　|　正文 333 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 warm 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1979 the porter wrote of ① a warm room in winter in the journal, and everybody in the coast said at once that it was ② warmer than the one named there the year before. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the porter, who never explained anything, had done it in public and gone home; it was the warm ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the warmest room in winter anybody in the coast had ever seen, or so the journal for August 1973 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too warm to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the visitor who had come to help; the warm ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the bag at the far cove, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a warm welcome at the door, and said that no visitor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as warm as the welcome at the door they had once had in the old coast. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was warm or not, and he said so.

By 1986 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the journal. What the line asked for was ⑦ something warm, and nothing besides. The visitor from the next coast called the whole plan ⑧ quite warm; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the journal kept the names of the warm ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1989, in silence, she wrote of another warm room in winter in the same journal, and the work, which took two weeks, seemed ⑨ warmer than anybody had expected. ⑩ The warmest welcome at the door in the whole coast, she said in 1991, was the one she could never quite name; the warm ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 温暖（前置定语 a warm room in winter：1979 年挑夫在行记里记下的那件温暖的房间）
B. adj. 温暖／热情（比较级 warmer than：文中两处，一处比冬天暖和的房间，一处比预想）
C. adj. 温暖／热情（最高级 the warmest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 温暖（表语 too warm to do：母亲觉得它太温暖，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 热情（前置定语 a warm welcome at the door：叔叔把整件事称作一桩热情的迎接）
F. adj. 热情（同级比较 as warm as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩门口热情的迎接相比）
G. adj. 热情（后置定语 something warm：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 热情（受程度副词修饰 quite warm：那位游客的评价）

items.q: the warmest room in winter anybody
a warm welcome at the door
The warmest welcome at the door in

answers.why: warm 意为“温暖”，1979 年挑夫在行记里记下的是“一件温暖的房间”，此处作前置定语 a warm room in winter。
warm 意为“温暖”，此处用比较级 warmer than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
warm 意为“温暖”，行记上 八月 那行字说它是海岸里最温暖的一件，故用最高级 the warmest room in winter。
warm 意为“温暖”，母亲认为这件东西“太温暖了，谁也用不上”，too warm to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
warm 意为“热情”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩热情的迎接”，此处作前置定语 a warm welcome at the door。
warm 意为“热情”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩门口热情的迎接一样热情”，同级比较用 as warm as。
warm 意为“热情”，行记上那半行字要的是“热情的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something warm。
warm 意为“热情”，邻海岸来的那位游客认为这套计划“相当热情”，quite 修饰原级 warm。
warm 意为“热情”，1989 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要热情”，故用比较级 warmer than。
warm 意为“热情”，母亲 1991 年说的是“整个海岸里最热情的那一桩”，故用最高级 the warmest welcome at the door。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1979 年，挑夫在行记里记下了一件温暖的房间。（a warm room in winter）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更温暖。（warmer than …）
母亲觉得它太温暖，谁也用不上。（too warm to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩热情的迎接。（a warm welcome at the door）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩门口热情的迎接一样热情。（as warm as …）
到了 1986 年，行记上只剩半行字：要的是一件热情的东西。（something warm）
answers: In 1979 the porter wrote of a warm room in winter in the journal.
Everybody said it was warmer than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too warm to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a warm welcome at the door.
He said nobody would call it as warm as the welcome at the door they had once had.
By 1986 the journal asked for nothing but something warm.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 warm 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1979 the porter wrote of a warm room in winter in the journal, and nobody forgot it.
It was the warmest room in winter in the coast, or so the journal says.
My mother thought it too warm to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a warm welcome at the door, and nobody argued with him.
The visitor from the next coast called the plan quite warm, and everybody laughed.
The warm ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
